title: Pseudo-coherent tensor tests imply relative pseudo-coherence
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a separated morphism of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. If $R\Gamma(X,E\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_X}K)$ is pseudo-coherent in $D(A)$ for every pseudo-coherent $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex, def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex, def-pc-derived-direct-image, def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], then $K$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Flatness, properness and Noetherian hypotheses are not required.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$. Apply the derived Chow neighbourhood lemma, obtaining $U,n,V,Z,z,E$; write $T=X\times_A P$, $P=\mathbf P^n_A$, and $p:T\to X$, $q:T\to P$. In particular $E$ is pseudo-coherent, $b^{-1}U=c^{-1}V$, $b$ is an isomorphism there, and $E$ has the stated graph-kernel restriction over $V$.

source.place: Tag 0CSL, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent, choice of derived Chow neighbourhood

proof.text: The projection $p$ is proper: it is the base change of $P\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, which is proper by the projective-space properness lemma. The Proj chart description identifies $D_+(x_i)$ with the spectrum of the degree-zero localization; its ring is $A[x_j/x_i:j\ne i]$, since every degree-zero fraction is a polynomial in these ratios and the monomials are independent. Formation of these rings over an affine base changes coefficients by tensor product. This also identifies this $P$ with the base-change projective-space interface used by the properness lemma. On a standard projective chart over any affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X$, $p$ is $\operatorname{Spec}B[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to\operatorname{Spec}B$. Thus it is flat by polynomial-projection flatness and locally finitely presented (the indicated polynomial presentation has finitely many generators and no relations); properness supplies quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. The same chart calculation shows $P\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, and hence its restriction $V\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, is flat and locally finitely presented. The other projection $q$ is separated and of finite type by separated finite-type base change applied to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$; in particular $q$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 0CSL, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent, geometry of the projections

proof.text: Set $F=Rq_*(Lp^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}E)$. It belongs to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(P)$: $E$ has quasi-coherent cohomology by pseudo-coherence; the affine-component pullback lemma gives quasi-coherence of $Lp^*K$ on every affine chart; choose a K-flat resolution of a representative of $Lp^*K$ and any representative of $E$; the recorded derived tensor is their total tensor complex, so the affine-component tensor lemma gives quasi-coherence of their derived tensor on every affine chart; and the qcqs direct-image lemma applies to $q$. The component assertions give the global ones because quasi-coherence is local, as in the definition of quasi-coherent cohomology.

source.place: Tag 0CSL, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent, domain of the projective-space criterion

proof.text: For $d=0,\ldots,n$, put $B_d=E\otimes^{\mathbf L}Lq^*\mathcal O_P(d)$ and $G_d=Rp_*B_d$. The pullback of the invertible twist is locally free of rank one: pull back a local trivialization of $\mathcal O_P(d)$. Tensoring a local bounded-above finite-free representative of $E$ with this line bundle has the same finite-free terms after trivializing the line bundle. Hence $B_d$ is pseudo-coherent. Applying flat proper finitely presented direct-image preservation to $p$ proves that $G_d$ is pseudo-coherent on $X$.

source.place: Tag 0CSL, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent, pseudo-coherence of the test objects

proof.text:
The projection formula for $q$, followed by composition of derived direct images, gives
$$R\Gamma(P,F\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_P(d))\simeq R\Gamma(T,Lp^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}B_d).$$
The projection formula for $p$ and the same composition comparison give
$$R\Gamma(T,Lp^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}B_d)\simeq R\Gamma(X,K\otimes^{\mathbf L}G_d).$$
The qcqs hypotheses for both projections were checked in step 2. All complexes used in these formulas have quasi-coherent cohomology: use the pseudo-coherent quasi-coherence lemma for $B_d,G_d$, and step 3 for the other factors. Associativity and symmetry of the recorded tensor put the factors in the displayed order. The hypothesis of the item, applied to $G_d$, makes the last object pseudo-coherent in $D(A)$; its invariance under isomorphism follows by composing the quasi-isomorphism from a bounded-above finite-free representative with the displayed isomorphism. The finite-twist criterion therefore shows $F$ is pseudo-coherent on $P$.

source.place: Tag 0CSL, lemma-characterize-pseudo-coherent, two projection-formula identifications and projective-space test

proof.text: The graph-kernel restriction lemma gives $F|_V\simeq Rj_*(K|_U)$ in $D(\mathcal O_V)$, where $j:U\hookrightarrow V$ is the closed immersion induced by $c$ using $b^{-1}U\simeq U$. Restricting a local bounded-above finite-free representative of $F$ proves $F|_V$ pseudo-coherent, and the displayed isomorphism proves the same for $Rj_*(K|_U)$. Since $V\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is flat and locally finitely presented, the flat-ambient criterion implies $K|_U$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $A$. As $x$ was arbitrary, these $U$ cover $X$. Relative pseudo-coherence is local on the source: since $K|_U$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ for each $U$ of this open covering of $X$, and $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally of finite type, $K$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $A$. (The charts of the different $U$ cannot simply be put together: the definition needs, over each member $V_a$ of one affine covering of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, charts covering all of the preimage of $V_a$; this is the content of the locality lemma.)
